sources.citation: Li et al., Solving the Set Packing Problem via a Maximum Weighted Independent Set Heuristic, Mathematical Problems in Engineering (2020), Article 3050714.
sources.use: Explicit conflict-graph encoding: mutually exclusive objects become adjacent and feasible packings are independent sets.

sources.citation: M.-C. Yang, J.J.M. Tan, L.-H. Hsu, Hamiltonian circuit and linear array embeddings in faulty k-ary n-cubes, Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing 67 (2007), 362–368.
sources.use: The k-ary n-cube is bipartite iff k is even; standard coordinate-neighbor torus framework.

sources.citation: P. Hall, On Representatives of Subsets, Journal of the London Mathematical Society 10 (1935), 26–30.
sources.use: Hall's marriage theorem; every finite regular bipartite graph has a perfect matching.

sources.citation: W.H. Haemers, Hoffman's ratio bound, Linear Algebra and its Applications 617 (2021), 215–219.
sources.use: The exact regular-graph eigenvalue upper bound for the independence number used in the Packing return.

sources.citation: A.S.A. Johnson, D.M. McClendon, Finite odometer factors of rank one Z^d-actions (2023), Lemma 2.7.
sources.use: For every Følner sequence in Z^d and every finite-index subgroup, each coset has asymptotic proportion 1/[Z^d:G].

sources.citation: C. Godsil, G. Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory, Springer (2001), §7.4.
sources.use: Graph-homomorphism inverse images of independent sets are independent; standard automorphism invariance.

sources.citation: I. van Heuven van Staereling, B. de Keijzer, G. Schäfer, The Ground-Set-Cost Budgeted Maximum Coverage Problem, MFCS 2016, LIPIcs 58, 50:1–50:13.
sources.use: Uses the standard equivalence 'incidence graph is a forest' = Berge-acyclic; supplies external hypergraph terminology for the Kakeya incidence object.

sources.citation: J. Oxley, Matroid Theory, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press (2011), circuits chapter.
sources.use: A circuit is a minimal dependent set; vector-matroid circuits formalize {e1,e2,e1+e2}.

sources.citation: Z. Dvir, On the size of Kakeya sets in finite fields, Journal of the American Mathematical Society 22(4) (2009), 1093–1097.
sources.use: Classical finite-field Kakeya requires a full line in every direction; its hypotheses are materially different from six fixed independent finite paths.

sources.citation: D.S. Dummit, R.M. Foote, Abstract Algebra, 3rd ed., Wiley (2004), group actions/orbit-stabilizer theorem.
sources.use: Orbit size equals group order divided by stabilizer size; makes the S4 24/6/4 count classical.

sources.citation: Standard finite-forest identity: for a finite forest with V vertices, E edges and c connected components, E=V-c; see any graph-theory text (e.g. Diestel, Graph Theory, 5th ed., Trees chapter).
sources.use: This identity converts Berge-acyclic incidence into the exact overlap defect and union-size formula.

sources.citation: One-to-one disjoint path covers on k-ary n-cubes, Theoretical Computer Science 412 (2011), 4513–4530.
sources.use: Standard k-ary n-cube coordinate model; explicitly records even-k bipartiteness and vertex/edge symmetry.
